newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Chariot dips, busy on Federal Mogul deal.
newsitem.headline: Chariot dips, busy on Federal Mogul deal.

text.p: Shares in South African motor firm Chariot Holdings Ltd slipped in busy early trade on Tuesday as investors rushed to take profits on confirmation it would buy businesses from U.S-based Federal-Mogul Corp.
By 0845 GMT shares had lost four cents to 113 cents in volume of almost 600,000 shares and the most active stock on the Johannesburg bourse. It earlier touched a low of 111 cents.
"It's the classic 'buy on rumour, sell on fact," a dealer said.
"The guys still like the shares, it's just that now the news has been announced," he said.

Chariot said earlier agreement had been reached to buy certain of the operations of Federal-Mogul, a U.S. vehicle spares firm. This follows speculation on such a buy which has sent the share on a roller-coaster ride.
On Monday Chariot stocks hit a new year high of 122 cents in morning trade before falling back to close at 117 cents.
